v.why: Coupled L2 under Adam sums shrinkage over many more parameters in wide layers, so the penalty dominates the normalized update; the opposite is plausible because wide nets are redundant and can absorb shrinkage without losing function.

Shrinkage compounds multiplicatively across three weight matrices and squeezes signal through each layer; alternatively, deeper nets overfit more on small tabular data, so extra L2 could help more there.

With the penalty scaled by 1/batch_size and many more updates per epoch, small batches see much stronger effective L2; conversely, small-batch nets are noisier and may overfit less, so an L2 increase could be benign there.

In standard parameterization the stable learning rate shrinks with width even under Adam, so widening at lr 0.278-1 pushes training into divergence; Adam's per-parameter normalization could instead make width irrelevant to stability, or wider nets could average out instability.

Gradient noise from small batches helps deeper, more nonconvex nets escape poor regions and regularizes their extra capacity; the opposite is plausible because noise compounds through layers and destabilizes deep training.

Heavy L2 on every added layer compounds into an output-scale collapse that the extra layer cannot overcome; alternatively, strong L2 may tame the overfitting that extra depth causes and make the added layer more useful.

Large batches give few updates in 243 epochs, and wider nets fit faster per step (closer to the lazy regime), substituting width for missing optimization steps; conversely, large-batch sharp minima in wide nets might generalize worse.

Wide layers sum more coordinated updates into each pre-activation, so a learning-rate increase overshoots more; Adam normalization could neutralize this, or wide nets could be smoother and tolerate higher rates.

Fewer steps at large batch leave the network undertrained, and a bigger learning rate substitutes for the missing steps (linear scaling); alternatively, Adam's normalized steps already make batch size and learning rate nearly decoupled.

At tiny learning rates the step count is the bottleneck, so cutting steps by enlarging the batch causes underfitting; conversely, low-noise large batches might let tiny learning rates make steadier progress.

Small-batch gradient noise combined with an already aggressive learning rate tips Adam into instability; the opposite is plausible because the noise could also help escape sharp regions that high learning rates fall into.

Deep ReLU nets realize their extra capacity only in a moderate learning-rate window, neither stalled nor divergent; alternatively, Adam could make depth gains insensitive to learning rate, so the mid band would not stand out.

Deeper nets have rougher loss landscapes where smaller steps avoid compounding layerwise overshoot; conversely, deep nets need larger learning rates to propagate signal within 243 epochs, so a decrease could hurt more.

With one hidden layer, width is the only capacity route, so narrowing is a direct bottleneck, whereas extra layers can substitute; alternatively, wide shallow nets may be over-capacity on these small datasets, so narrowing would cost little.

Small nets underfit, so L2 binds them hardest and relaxing it frees scarce capacity; the opposite is plausible because conventional wisdom says only large overfitting-prone nets are sensitive to regularization.

Because the penalty gradient scales with 1/batch_size, larger batches dilute an over-strong L2, so the batch increase partly undoes over-regularization; alternatively, fewer steps at large batch could compound the underfitting caused by heavy L2.

With almost no explicit L2, large-learning-rate implicit regularization substitutes for the missing penalty; conversely, without L2 to bound weight norms, higher learning rates could let weights grow and destabilize.
Narrow deep ReLU stacks bottleneck through dead units and lose information layer by layer; alternatively, depth could substitute for missing width and add the capacity narrow nets lack.

Small-batch gradient noise provides regularization that substitutes for absent L2, while with ample L2 it is redundant; conversely, at low alpha the noise might amplify fitting of noisy labels instead.

Shallow nets have better-conditioned landscapes that tolerate and benefit from larger steps, while deep nets compound overshoot; alternatively, shallow nets may already converge at mid learning rate, leaving no gain from going higher.

## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Common assumption | Negation | Conditional effect if the negation holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Under Adam, the L2 penalty acts the same regardless of network size. | Coupled L2 adds up over all weights. Adam's per-parameter normalization lets the penalty take over the update direction in large networks. | An alpha step up hurts more when width is high or depth is 3. |
| A2 | Alpha and batch size are independent knobs. | In an sklearn-style MLP the penalty gradient is scaled by 1/batch_size. Small batches therefore get a stronger effective L2, and they also take many more penalized steps over 243 epochs. | An alpha step up hurts more at low batch size. A batch-size step up helps more when alpha is high. |
| A3 | Adam's normalization makes the best learning rate independent of width. | Wide ReLU networks in standard parameterization still blow up at large learning rates. | A width step up turns harmful at high learning rate. A learning-rate step up hurts more when width is high. |
| A4 | Extra depth is a fixed capacity gain. | Depth interacts with gradient noise, which helps escape poor regions, and with L2 shrinkage that compounds across layers. | A depth step up helps more at low batch size and less at high alpha. |
| A5 | Learning rate and batch size can each be tuned on their own. | With fixed epochs, a large batch means fewer steps. Too small a learning rate then leaves the network undertrained, and a small batch combined with a large learning rate diverges. | A learning-rate step up helps more at high batch size. A batch-size step up hurts at low learning rate. A batch-size step down hurts at high learning rate. |
| A6 | Regularization sources do not substitute for one another. | Small-batch noise and large-learning-rate noise act as implicit regularizers. | Extra noise helps more when alpha is low. |
| A7 | Width and depth are interchangeable sources of capacity. | Width is the only capacity route in a 1-layer network, and narrow deep ReLU networks bottleneck through dead units. | A width step down hurts more at depth 1. A depth step up helps less at low width. |
| A8 | Removing regularization mostly matters for big networks. | Small networks underfit, so L2 binds them hardest. | An alpha step down helps more at low width. |
